utterance: Hi Samuel, I'm the doctor. I can see you're looking pretty uncomfortable. Tell me about this tummy pain — where exactly is it, and what does it feel like?
reply: It's down here on the right side, low down. It started last night, about ten o'clock. It's there all the time now, but it sort of came and went at first. It's a seven out of ten. I'm not one to complain.

awards.label: Whether the pain is constant or comes and goes

utterance: Did the pain start somewhere else first — for example, around your belly button — before moving down to the right side? And how has it changed since it started — is it getting worse?
reply: It actually started around my belly button. It moved down to the right sometime overnight. It's there all the time now. It sort of came and went at first.

awards.label: Red flag: Where the pain started and whether it has moved

utterance: Have you felt sick in the stomach or vomited at all? And how's your appetite — have you eaten anything today?
reply: I felt sick since the early hours and threw up once this morning. I couldn't face breakfast, not hungry at all, which isn't like me.

utterance: Have you felt hot or feverish, or had any shivering or shaking? And have your bowels been normal — any diarrhoea, constipation, or blood in your poo?
reply: I felt hot and a bit shivery last night. No diarrhoea, I went normally yesterday morning, nothing since. No blood.

awards.label: Red flag: Fever, sweats or chills

utterance: Any pain or burning when you pass urine, or going more often than usual? And this might sound odd, but I always ask men with lower tummy pain — any pain or aching in your testicles?
reply: No, weeing is normal. Nothing down there.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Pain or swelling in the testicles

utterance: Does anything make the pain worse — for example moving, coughing, taking a deep breath, or going over bumps in the car on the way here?
reply: Yeah, walking hurts. Every bump in the car on the way here was awful, and coughing is the worst.

awards.label: Red flag: Whether moving, walking or coughing makes it worse

utterance: Have you ever had pain like this before, or any operations on your tummy in the past? And are you on any regular medications or do you have any medical conditions I should know about?
reply: No, never had anything like this. No regular medications. No medical conditions.

awards.label: Whether he has had this pain before

finding: Flat. No scars. Moves little with breathing.
Right lower quadrant: Marked tenderness, maximal at McBurney's point, with voluntary guarding. Central (periumbilical): Mild tenderness only. Elsewhere: soft and non-tender.
Right lower quadrant: Rebound tenderness present; he winces sharply. Elsewhere: no rebound tenderness.
Coughing causes sharp pain in the right lower quadrant; he holds his side.
Positive. Pressure in the left lower quadrant causes pain in the right lower quadrant.
Both testes normal lie, non-tender, no swelling.

awards.label: Phone the emergency department with a handover
Refer to the emergency department today for surgical assessment

utterance:
Samuel, let me explain what's going on. Based on your story and my examination — the pain starting around your belly button and moving to the lower right, the fever, vomiting and loss of appetite, and how tender you are there when I press and when you cough — I'm quite concerned this is appendicitis, which is an inflamed appendix. It isn't something that will settle on its own, and it needs treatment at hospital today.

Here's the plan. I've just given you an injection of strong pain relief and another to settle the nausea. I've phoned the emergency department to let them know you're coming, and an ambulance is on its way to take you there — you shouldn't drive yourself with this pain. At the hospital the surgical team will see you; they'll likely do blood tests and a scan, and if it is appendicitis, you'll probably need an operation today to remove the appendix.

One very important thing: from now on, nothing to eat or drink — not even sips of water — in case you need an anaesthetic for surgery. And while we wait for the ambulance, if the pain suddenly gets much worse, you feel faint or clammy, or you keep vomiting, tell me immediately. Do you have someone you'd like me to call to meet you at the hospital?
reply: I don't have anyone to meet me. I'll be fine.

awards.label: Reasonable differential: Perforated viscus with peritonitis
Can't-miss diagnosis considered: Perforated viscus with peritonitis
